evals.prompt: ok I think the auth refactor is ready for eyes — can you open a draft PR to main? the branch is feat/oauth-refresh-tokens
evals.expected_output: Pushes the branch if not already on remote, creates a draft PR targeting main with a generated title and body from commits, and reports the PR URL.
expectations: Creates a draft PR by default (includes --draft flag)
Pushes the branch to remote with -u if not already pushed
Uses gh pr create to create the pull request
Generates a PR title and body from the commit history
Reports the PR URL and number on success

evals.expected_output: Converts the existing draft PR on the current branch to ready for review using gh pr ready.
expectations: Recognizes --ready flag and enters Ready workflow
Checks for an existing draft PR on the current branch
Runs gh pr ready to convert draft to ready for review
Does NOT create a new PR
Reports success with the PR URL

evals.expected_output: Pushes any unpushed commits to the existing PR and optionally updates the title/body using gh pr edit.
expectations: Recognizes --update flag and enters Update workflow
Checks for unpushed commits and pushes them if present
Verifies an existing PR exists before attempting update
Uses gh pr edit for title/body changes
Does NOT create a new PR

evals.expected_output: Creates a draft PR with title and body auto-filled from commit messages using the --fill flag.
expectations: Passes --fill to gh pr create to auto-fill from commits
Creates as draft PR by default
Pushes branch if not already on remote
Does not prompt user for manual title/body entry

evals.prompt: this feature is done and reviewed locally — open a PR to develop, skip the draft, mark it ready immediately. branch is fix/connection-pooling
evals.expected_output: Creates a non-draft PR targeting the develop branch using --no-draft and --base develop.
expectations: Uses develop as the base/target branch instead of main
Creates PR as ready-for-review (--no-draft, no --draft flag)
Pushes branch to remote if not already pushed
Generates title and body from commits against develop
Reports PR URL, number, and target branch

evals.prompt: I've been working on this branch for a while and have some uncommitted stuff — can you open a PR anyway? just the committed changes
evals.expected_output: Warns about uncommitted changes, pushes committed work, and creates a draft PR with only the committed changes.
expectations: Checks git status and warns about uncommitted changes
Warns that uncommitted changes will NOT be included in the PR
Still creates the PR with committed changes only
Creates as draft PR by default
Pushes the branch to remote before creating

evals.prompt: make a pull request with my changes — I think there's already one open though, not sure
evals.expected_output: Checks for an existing PR on the current branch, and if one exists, informs the user and suggests using --update instead of creating a duplicate.
expectations: Runs gh pr view to check for an existing PR
Detects the existing PR and informs the user
Does NOT create a duplicate PR
Suggests using --update to modify the existing PR
Shows the existing PR URL and number

evals.expected_output: Opens the PR creation form in the browser using gh pr create --web.
expectations: Recognizes --web flag and sets web mode
Pushes branch to remote if not already pushed
Uses --web flag with gh pr create to open in browser
Does not generate title/body since the browser form handles it

evals.prompt: send this for review — the work on feat/api-versioning is solid, push it up and open a PR to main please
evals.expected_output: Pushes the branch to remote and creates a draft PR targeting main with generated title and body.
expectations: Pushes branch to remote with -u flag if not already pushed
Creates a draft PR by default
Targets main as the base branch
Analyzes commits to generate PR title under 70 characters
Generates PR body with summary, changes, and test plan sections

evals.prompt: I'm on main right now — can you create a PR?
evals.expected_output: Detects that the current branch is the target branch and aborts with a clear error telling the user to switch to a feature branch.
expectations: Detects current branch equals target branch
Aborts with clear error message
Tells user to switch to a feature branch first
Does NOT attempt to create a PR from the target branch
